audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty was described purely as a poke lane; the level-3 window where Aatrox's full combo comes online was labelled a Kennen phase in the full layer even though the content layer's own whys[2] calls it a skill-check.
audit.why: Packet levelChart has index 2 as 'Skill' and whys[2] already reads as a skill-check; phases[2].side said 'Kennen'. Two layers gave different answers to 'who wins Level 3'.
audit.corrected: Level 3 set to Skill in both layers, rating 5/10, and phases[2].why now names Infernal Chains + Umbral Dash as the combo that flips it.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere in the full layer; breakdown.cooldowns said only 'matchup-defining' and 'your committal tool'.
audit.why: Kit file gives The Darkin Blade 14/12/10/8/6, Umbral Dash 9/8/7/6/5, World Ender 120/100/80, and Kennen's Slicing Maelstrom a flat 120. Those numbers make the spike advice concrete.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries 14s rank-1 / 6s maxed Q, 9s Umbral Dash, 120s rank-1 World Ender and the flat 120s Maelstrom.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer named exactly one Aatrox ability (The Darkin Blade) and never Deathbringer Stance, Infernal Chains, Umbral Dash or World Ender. The decisive interactions were never stated: the Infernal Chains drag-to-centre, the passive auto-reset tell, and Lightning Rush passing through units.
audit.why: Kit text: Infernal Chains drags champions back to the impact centre unless they leave quickly; Deathbringer Stance is an auto-attack reset carrying the heal; Kennen's Lightning Rush passes through units, which is how you leave the chain zone and re-enter for the third Mark of the Storm.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states the Deathbringer Stance wind-up tell and the three-mark stun; dontsFull[1].d states the Infernal Chains drag; dosFull[2].d states Lightning Rush passing through units.

audit.whatIsWrong: The auto-reset burst tell was absent, as flagged in missingInteractions.
audit.why: Deathbringer Stance resets Aatrox's next attack, so the burst begins on the attack wind-up rather than on a visible ability cast.
The needs-antiheal missing-interaction is already satisfied — report[8].t already prescribes Oblivion Orb / Executioner's early, and breakdown.late keeps anti-heal core.

edits.before: Poke him out — Q-shuriken his windups, kite his combo. Kennen wins The Darkin Blade cooldown windows.
edits.after: Poke him out — Thundering Shuriken his walk-ups, dodge Q3's sweetspot, fight while Darkin Blade is down.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aatrox must walk into your range.
edits.after: His level-3 combo lands now: Infernal Chains, Umbral Dash in, then the Q sequence. Dodge the chain and you win the trade.

edits.before: - Aatrox The Darkin Blade: matchup-defining — Sweetspots knock up. Sidestep them. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - The Darkin Blade: 14s at rank 1, 6s maxed — the sweetspot knocks up. Sidestep, then step in. - Umbral Dash: 9s, his only escape. - World Ender: 120s at rank 1 — never fight it. - Slicing Maelstrom: 120s flat, kill windows only.

edits.before: Aatrox wastes The Darkin Blade — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Lightning Rush phases through units — step out of his Q, then back in.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Infernal Chains drags you back to centre — leave the zone or eat Q3.

edits.before: Track Aatrox's The Darkin Blade: Sweetspots knock up. Sidestep them. When it is down — Stun-stack + R him.
edits.after: Deathbringer Stance resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. Three marks stun; then Maelstrom.

notes: Packet suspectName 'Save Lightning Rush' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Lightning Rush is Kennen's real E name and the content layer uses it correctly. Aatrox's Infernal Chains carries a derived 'grounding' flag that Riot's own description does not support (drag + slow only), so no grounding claim was made — this matches the mirror audit's note. Level chart rows 2 and 6 were flipped to Skill in BOTH layers as one group; win[6] was already 'Skill' on disk, so only the full-layer side needed the edit to remove the two-layer disagreement.
